compute_fairness.policy: equal_declared_compute_budget_per_candidate_and_benchmark_case; no candidate may receive extra attempts, parallelism, retries, cache advantage, or privileged data
compute_fairness.budgets: Each benchmark suite declares wall_clock_limit_seconds, cpu_time_limit_seconds, gpu_time_limit_seconds_when_available, memory_limit_bytes, energy_limit_when_measurable, concurrency, retry_limit, warmup_count, measured_repetitions, and timeout_behavior before any candidate run.

environments.description: Verified local laptop runner; record exact hardware, OS, power mode, runtime/compiler, memory, thermal state and available accelerator.
Pinned GitHub-hosted runner image and instance class; record actual runner metadata and available accelerators.

compute_fairness.comparison: Compare candidates directly only inside a matched hardware cohort. Laptop and GitHub results are separate cohorts unless a documented calibration method justifies normalization. Allocate the same declared time and resource caps to every candidate within each cohort.
anti_cheating: Freeze candidate commit SHA, build flags, model/tokenizer/data hashes, benchmark version and configuration before each campaign.
Use identical task packets, prompt/tool context, input order policy, seeds, evaluation split, quality/safety gates and output limits.
Predeclare warmups, measured repetitions, retry policy, timeouts, cache policy, concurrency and network access.
Separate cold-start and warm-cache results; never mix them in one score.
Use hidden holdouts and independent scoring; candidate code cannot read evaluator labels or modify score aggregation.
No manual per-candidate tuning after seeing holdout results; changes require a new versioned campaign.
Publish all eligible, failed, timed-out and cancelled attempts; do not omit unfavorable runs.

Capture runner image, CPU/GPU model, RAM, compiler/runtime versions, power/thermal state when available, utilization, peak memory, throughput, latency percentiles, energy where measurable, cost and logs.
compute_fairness.selection: No candidate wins by language, repository, hardware brand, or parameter count. Hard gates first, then multi-objective score with uncertainty and reproducible evidence.

training.training_authority: canonical_python_training_pipeline; runtimes consume only approved, versioned artifacts unless separately certified

resource_catalog.purpose: Vendor-neutral discovery and governed access to AI training, evaluation, teacher, tokenizer and compute resources; discovery never implies download or training permission.

source_families.review: Per-model and per-dataset license, terms, provenance and intended-use review required.
Verify dataset terms, research restrictions, benchmark license and train/evaluation contamination.
Verify source-specific license, privacy, robots/collection constraints, attribution and derivative-use rights.

examples: GitHub repositories with explicit compatible licenses
source_families.review: Respect repository licenses, source attribution, secrets/PII screening and code provenance.
Require ownership/authority, purpose-specific consent, retention, revocation and tenant isolation.
Pin immutable revisions; verify output-use, distillation, retention, classification and provider terms.
Pin versions, verify hardware compatibility, license, reproducibility, isolation and budget.

resource_catalog.ingestion_gate: Discover metadata → owner rights/privacy review → staged immutable manifest → quality/PII/contamination checks → approved storage → explicit compute approval → training/evaluation. No crawler or adapter may auto-download or train by discovery alone.
resource_catalog.ranking: Rank resources by task relevance, rights certainty, provenance, quality, freshness, representativeness, privacy class, contamination risk, format, tokenizer/model compatibility, compute cost and reproducibility.

contents: verified license and training-use rights evidence
shared_catalog.access: Shared metadata is discoverable by Buddy; raw data is not implicitly shared.

division_isolation.default: Each division owns its dataset versions, train/validation/test manifests, private holdouts, derived examples, checkpoints, weights, tokenizer snapshots, database namespace, object-store prefix and access grants.
division_isolation.cross_division_reuse: Only explicitly approved, rights-cleared datasets or derived artifacts may be shared. Record source division, recipient division, purpose, transformation, approval, hashes and expiry.
division_isolation.forbidden: No default cross-division raw private-data access, private-holdout reuse, secret transfer, or mixing train/evaluation splits across divisions.

data_governance.shared_corpora: A centrally curated, rights-cleared common corpus may be mounted read-only by multiple divisions using immutable version/hash references; division-specific transformations and splits remain separately versioned.
data_governance.buddy_access: Buddy queries the shared catalog and selects only sources/models whose rights, privacy classification, domain fit, freshness, quality and compute constraints satisfy the task. Access to bytes requires an authorized data-plane grant.
data_governance.privacy: Tenant/division isolation and purpose-specific user consent remain mandatory; metadata visibility never grants content access.
